Weide.et: From Middle High German weide, from Old High German weida, from Proto-West Germanic *waiþu, from Proto-Germanic *waiþō. Cognate to Dutch weide (“pasture”).

From Middle High German wīde, from Old High German wīda, from Proto-Germanic *wīþijō (“willow”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéh₁itis (“that which twines or bends, branch, switch”). Cognate to Dutch wijde (“willow”), Swedish vide, English withy.

Weidmann.et: From Weide (“pasture, hunting”) + Mann (“man”). Cognate to Dutch weidman (“hunter”).

s: Weiden in der Oberpfalz (an independent town in the Upper Palatinate region, Bavaria, Germany)
Cattle were grazing in the field.
Sie weidet sich am Pech ihrer Rivalin.
She gloats over her rival's bad luck.
weiden.et: From Middle High German weiden, from Old High German weidōn, from a derivative of Proto-West Germanic *waiþu (“pasture, grassland”).

t: Ein Schäferhund treibt eine Schafherde zur Weide.
A sheep dog drives the flock to the pasture.
Der Schäfer führte seine Herde zur Weide.
The shepherd led his flock to pasture.
Diese Weide sieht wie ein Mammut aus.
This willow-tree looks like a mammoth.
Maria saß flötespielend im Schatten einer Weide.
Mary sat in the shade of a willow tree playing her flute.
l: Bei einem Spurwechsel kam es in der Brenner-Schäfer-Straße in Weiden zum Zusammenstoß.
Das erste Mal draußen: Lämmer auf der Weide in List auf Sylt.
